content: The UCLA School of Public Health is a graduate-level institution dedicated to public health education and research. It is affiliated with the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and is situated within the Center for Health Sciences building on the UCLA campus, which is located in the Westwood neighborhood of Los Angeles, California. The current dean of the school is Linda Rosenstock, MD, MPH. The school boasts a network of over 8,000 alumni and employs 80 full-time faculty members. Its student body is diverse, with individuals hailing from more than 35 countries. History UCLA began offering undergraduate courses in public health in 1946. For the subsequent 15 years, public health education at UCLA was part of a system-wide University of California public health school. In 1957, UCLA initiated a program that allowed students to pursue advanced degrees in public health. The UCLA School of Public Health was officially established on March 17, 1961, with Lenor S. (Steve) Goerke serving as its inaugural dean. In 2003, the school introduced an undergraduate minor in public health. Departments and Degrees The UCLA School of Public Health offers degrees across several departments, including: Biostatistics: Degrees offered include MPH, MS, PhD, and DrPH. Community Health Sciences: Degrees offered include MPH, MS, PhD, and DrPH. Environmental Health Sciences: Degrees offered include MPH, MS, PhD, and DrPH. Epidemiology: Degrees offered include MPH, MS, PhD, and DrPH. Health Services: Degrees offered include MPH, MS, PhD, and DrPH. Additionally, the school offers two interdepartmental degrees: Environmental Science & Engineering: Doctor of Environmental Science and Engineering (DEnv). Molecular Toxicology: PhD. The school also provides joint degree programs in collaboration with other UCLA graduate schools, including: MPH/MA in African Studies MPH/MA in Asian American Studies MPH/MA in Islamic Studies MPH/MA in Latin American Studies MPH/JD with the School of Law MPH/MBA with the School of Management MPH/MD with the School of Medicine Research Centers The UCLA School of Public Health sponsors or is affiliated with several research centers, including: Center for Adolescent Health Promotion Division of Cancer Prevention and Control Research Center for Public Health and Disasters Center for Environmental Genomics Centers for Environmental Quality and Health Center to Eliminate Health Disparities Center for Healthier Children, Families, and Communities UCLA Center for Health Policy Research Center for Human Nutrition Southern California Injury Prevention Research Center Notable Alumni For a comprehensive list of notable alumni, refer to the UCLA Alumni Hall of Fame. Notable Faculty Abdelmonem A. Afifi: Dean of the School of Public Health (1985–2000). Roslyn Alfin-Slater: Demonstrated that dietary cholesterol does not raise serum cholesterol levels. Lester Breslow: Dean of the School of Public Health (1972–1980); former president of the American Public Health Association. E. Richard Brown: Former president of the American Public Health Association. Roger Detels: Dean of the School of Public Health (1980–1985); identified mechanisms of HIV-related immune deficiency transmission among homosexual men. Gladys Emerson: Conducted research leading to the isolation and discovery of the nutritional value of vitamin E. Jonathan Fielding: Director of Public Health and Health Officer for Los Angeles County. Derek and Patrice Jelliffe: Advocated for the global promotion of breastfeeding benefits. Lenor S. (Steve) Goerke: Founding dean of the School of Public Health (1961–1972). Milton Roemer: Renowned health systems researcher; known for Roemer's law, which states that in a fully insured population, any hospital bed built will be filled. Ruth Roemer: Former president of the American Public Health Association. Linda Rosenstock: Current dean of the School of Public Health (2000–present). John Froines: Professor of environmental health sciences, former Director of Toxic Substances for the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, and member of the Chicago Seven.
